product.benefits.title: What you can build with Fission
product.catalog.title: Explore the platform
product.overview.title: One Rust application model, many ways to ship.
product.overview.summary: Build desktop, mobile, Web, terminal and server-rendered products with typed components and shared state. Fission carries one product model through development, testing and release.
product.overview.benefit.1: Reuse product data, reducers and Compose components across targets; generate only the platform shell each target needs.
product.overview.benefit.2: Keep retained interface state beside its component and shared product truth in GlobalState.
product.overview.benefit.3: Build crawlable static and server-rendered sites with route metadata, Markdown and interactive WebAssembly previews.
product.overview.image_alt: Fission widget gallery showing a shared Rust component interface
product.cross_platform.title: Ship one Rust app to desktop, mobile and Web.
product.cross_platform.summary: Keep product rules and Compose views in shared Rust code. Fission generates target shells for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android, iOS and Web.
product.cross_platform.benefit.1: Share reducers, routes and product data instead of rebuilding the same feature for each host.
product.cross_platform.benefit.2: Use target-specific shells and capabilities when a device needs native behaviour.
product.cross_platform.benefit.3: Check narrow touch layouts and desktop workflows without splitting the app model.
product.cross_platform.image_alt: Fission inbox interface adapted to a narrow mobile screen
product.terminal.title: Build terminal interfaces with the Fission app model.
product.terminal.summary: Author terminal screens with the same typed components, state transitions and product data used in graphical Fission apps.
product.terminal.benefit.1: Keep keyboard navigation and terminal input in the same reducer-driven app model.
product.terminal.benefit.2: Reuse product state and app rules when a terminal workflow belongs beside a desktop or Web app.
product.terminal.benefit.3: Run and package a terminal target through Fission's project commands.
product.static_sites.title: Build crawlable websites in Rust.
product.static_sites.summary: Compose responsive pages in Rust and combine them with Markdown content. Fission writes static HTML with route metadata and deployable assets.
product.static_sites.benefit.1: Give each page a descriptive title, summary and canonical URL for search and sharing.
product.static_sites.benefit.2: Generate a sitemap, robots rules and searchable content as part of the site build.
product.static_sites.benefit.3: Put long-form guides in Markdown and reuse Fission components for navigation and page layouts.
product.static_sites.image_alt: Fission text interface example used as a static-site preview
product.server_sites.title: Send useful HTML before the browser runs app code.
product.server_sites.summary: Render route content on the server, then add typed actions and focused WebAssembly islands where a page needs interaction.
product.server_sites.benefit.1: Keep the first response useful for people, assistive technology and search crawlers.
product.server_sites.benefit.2: Run database and host work asynchronously through jobs, services and capabilities.
product.server_sites.benefit.3: Add validation, loading, error and success feedback around real server actions.
product.server_sites.image_alt: Fission inbox composition screen with a focused form workflow
product.lifecycle.title: Carry the same project from first build to release.
product.lifecycle.summary: Use Fission's project commands to check targets, build packages and make the steps between a working app and a shipped app easier to follow.
product.lifecycle.benefit.1: See target requirements and missing configuration before they block a release.
product.lifecycle.benefit.2: Keep repeatable build and packaging steps beside the project that owns them.
product.lifecycle.benefit.3: Use the CLI reference to choose the next build, test or distribution command.
product.tools.title: Trace a user action to the output your app ships.
product.tools.summary: Inspect state, reducers, layout, semantics, resources, screenshots and device logs through the model the application actually runs.
product.tools.benefit.1: Compare the rendered interface with the state and actions that produced it.
product.tools.benefit.2: Use semantics and live UI tests to check keyboard, touch and assistive navigation.
product.tools.benefit.3: Find target-specific problems before packaging, with diagnostics tied to Fission project workflows.
product.tools.image_alt: Fission widget gallery used to inspect component behaviour
product.design.title: Keep design decisions consistent across every target.
product.design.summary: Generate typed Rust from Design System Package JSON, then read the same colours, spacing, typography and component styles from every Fission shell.
product.design.benefit.1: Catch token and component changes during the build instead of parsing design JSON at runtime.
product.design.benefit.2: Select themes through Env and keep app-controlled theme choices in GlobalState.
product.design.benefit.3: Share visual rules across Web, desktop and mobile while adapting layouts to each screen.
product.design.image_alt: Fission widget gallery showing consistent component styling
product.charts.title: Show product data without adding another UI stack.
product.charts.summary: Build dashboards from typed Rust data. Fission charts share the app's theme, semantics, interactions and target delivery.
product.charts.benefit.1: Choose typed axes and series for comparisons, trends, distributions and relationships.
product.charts.benefit.2: Connect selection and chart events to the same reducers used by the rest of your app.
product.charts.benefit.3: Keep chart colours and typography aligned with the active design system.
product.charts.image_alt: Fission chart gallery showing several data visualisations
